# JDK calls that read the JVM default time zone. A decoder's result must not depend on it (#141),
# so the forbiddenapis plugin (configured in the parent POM) fails the build on any of them.
# Pass an explicit ZoneId or ZoneOffset instead, or keep the value in a java.time type that
# needs no zone.
#
# Do not edit this list by guesswork. DefaultTimeZoneApiAuditTest walks the JDK bytecode back
# from TimeZone.getDefaultRef, TimeZone.getDefault, ZoneId.systemDefault and
# Clock.systemDefaultZone and fails when a reader is missing here; add what it reports. Whole
# packages are listed where a decoder has no use for any of the package.
#
# Some entries read the zone only in a corner case, such as java.util.Date#equals, which
# normalizes a Date changed through its deprecated setters in the default zone. They are banned
# anyway: a decoder has no need for them, and telling the corner case apart from the ordinary
# path is the guesswork this list avoids.

@defaultMessage Reads the JVM default time zone; pass an explicit ZoneId

java.util.logging.**
javax.management.**
javax.print.**
javax.security.auth.**
javax.swing.**
